18: function matchRoutes(routeConfig: RouteConfig[], pathname: string) {

20:   // component, but we load route components with string paths.

27:   resolvedLink: string;
28:   anchor: boolean;
29: };

31: type BrokenLinksMap = {[pathname: string]: BrokenLink[]};

33: // The linking data that has been collected on Docusaurus pages during SSG
34: // {rendered page pathname => links and anchors collected on that page}
35: type CollectedLinks = {
36:   [pathname: string]: {links: string[]; anchors: string[]};
37: };
38: 
39: // We use efficient data structures for performance reasons
40: // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
41: type CollectedLinksNormalized = Map<
42:   string,
43:   {links: Set<string>; anchors: Set<string>}
44: >;

46: class BrokenLinkAnalyzer {
47:   private readonly collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
48: 
49:   constructor(collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized) {
50:     this.collectedLinks = collectedLinks;
51:   }
52: 
53:   collectBrokenLinks(
54:     routes: RouteConfig[],
55:     routeCatalog: RouteMatchCatalog,
56:   ): BrokenLinksMap {
57:     const validPathnames = new Set(this.collectedLinks.keys());
58: 
59:     // IMPORTANT: this is an optimization
60:     // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
61:     // Matching against the route array can be expensive
62:     // If the route is already in the valid pathnames,
63:     // we can avoid matching against it
64:     const remainingRoutes = (function filterRoutes() {
65:       // Goal: unit tests should behave the same with this enabled or disabled
66:       const disableOptimization = false;
67:       if (disableOptimization) {
68:         return routes;
69:       }
70:       const otherRoutes: RouteConfig[] = [];
71:       routeCatalog.candidates.forEach((candidate, index) => {
72:         const route = routes[index]!;
73:         if (candidate.exact && validPathnames.has(candidate.path)) {
74:           if (!candidate.strict) {
75:             const slashForm = routeCatalog.createSlashForm(candidate.path);
76:             validPathnames.add(slashForm.withSlash);
77:             validPathnames.add(slashForm.withoutSlash);
78:           }
79:         } else {
80:           otherRoutes.push(route);
81:         }
82:       });
83:       return otherRoutes;
84:     })();
85: 
86:     function isPathnameMatchingAnyRoute(pathname: string): boolean {
87:       if (matchRoutes(remainingRoutes, pathname).length > 0) {
88:         // IMPORTANT: this is an optimization
89:         // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
90:         // Large Docusaurus sites have many routes!
91:         // We try to minimize calls to a possibly expensive matchRoutes function
92:         validPathnames.add(pathname);
93:         return true;
94:       }
95: 
96:       return false;
97:     }

99:     const result: BrokenLinksMap = {};
100:     this.collectedLinks.forEach((_unused, pagePath) => {
101:       try {
102:         const pageData = this.collectedLinks.get(pagePath)!;
103:         const pageAnchors = new CollectedPageAnchors(pagePath, pageData);
104:         const pageLinks = pageAnchors.pageLinks;
105:         const brokenLinks: BrokenLink[] = [];
106:         pageLinks.links.forEach((link) => {
107:           const parsed = parseURLPath(link, pageAnchors.pathname);
108:           const linkTarget = new ParsedLinkTarget(
109:             parsed.pathname,
110:             parsed.search,
111:             parsed.hash,
112:           );
113:           const resolvedLink = `${linkTarget.pathname}${
114:             linkTarget.search === undefined ? '' : `?${linkTarget.search}`
115:           }${linkTarget.hash === undefined ? '' : `#${linkTarget.hash}`}`;
116:           const pathnames = [
117:             linkTarget.pathname,
118:             decodeURI(linkTarget.pathname),
119:           ];
120:           const isPathBroken =
121:             !pathnames.some((p) => validPathnames.has(p)) &&
122:             !pathnames.some(isPathnameMatchingAnyRoute);
123:           if (isPathBroken) {
124:             brokenLinks.push({
125:               link,
126:               resolvedLink,
127:               anchor: false,
128:             });
129:             return;
130:           }
131:           const {pathname, hash} = linkTarget;
132:           // Link has no hash: it can't be a broken anchor link
133:           if (hash === undefined) {
134:             return;
135:           }
136:           // Link has empty hash ("#", "/page#"...): we do not report it as broken
137:           // Empty hashes are used for various weird reasons, by us and other users...
138:           // See for example: https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/pull/6003
139:           if (hash === '') {
140:             return;
141:           }
142:           const targetPage =
143:             this.collectedLinks.get(pathname) ||
144:             this.collectedLinks.get(decodeURI(pathname));
145:           // link with anchor to a page that does not exist (or did not collect any
146:           // link/anchor) is considered as a broken anchor
147:           if (!targetPage) {
148:             brokenLinks.push({
149:               link,
150:               resolvedLink,
151:               anchor: true,
152:             });
153:             return;
154:           }
155:           const isSelfTarget =
156:             pageAnchors.pathname === pathname ||
157:             pageAnchors.pathname === decodeURI(pathname);
158:           const targetAnchors = isSelfTarget
159:             ? pageAnchors.anchors
160:             : targetPage.anchors;
161:           // it's a not broken anchor if the anchor exists on the target page
162:           if (
163:             targetAnchors.has(hash) ||
164:             targetAnchors.has(decodeURIComponent(hash))
165:           ) {
166:             return;
167:           }
168:           brokenLinks.push({
169:             link,
170:             resolvedLink,
171:             anchor: true,
172:           });
173:         });
174:         result[pagePath] = brokenLinks;
175:       } catch (e) {
176:         throw new Error(`Unable to get broken links for page ${pagePath}.`, {
177:           cause: e,

180:     });
181:     return result;

188:  * reason, we only consider the "final routes" that do not have subroutes.

191: function filterIntermediateRoutes(routesInput: RouteConfig[]): RouteConfig[] {
192:   const routesWithout404 = routesInput.filter((route) => route.path !== '*');
193:   return flattenRoutes(routesWithout404);
194: }

196: function getBrokenLinks({
197:   collectedLinks,
198:   routes,
199: }: {
200:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
201:   routes: RouteConfig[];
202: }): BrokenLinksMap {
203:   const filteredRoutes = filterIntermediateRoutes(routes);
204:   const analyzer = new BrokenLinkAnalyzer(collectedLinks);
205:   return analyzer.collectBrokenLinks(
206:     filteredRoutes,
207:     new RouteMatchCatalog(filteredRoutes),

211: function brokenLinkMessage(brokenLink: BrokenLink): string {
212:   const showResolvedLink = brokenLink.link !== brokenLink.resolvedLink;
213:   return `${brokenLink.link}${
214:     showResolvedLink ? ` (resolved as: ${brokenLink.resolvedLink})` : ''
215:   }`;

218: function createBrokenLinksMessage(
219:   pagePath: string,
220:   brokenLinks: BrokenLink[],
221: ): string {
222:   const type = brokenLinks[0]?.anchor === true ? 'anchor' : 'link';
223: 
224:   const anchorMessage =
225:     brokenLinks.length > 0
226:       ? `- Broken ${type} on source page path = ${pagePath}:
227:    -> linking to ${brokenLinks
228:      .map(brokenLinkMessage)
229:      .join('\n   -> linking to ')}`
230:       : '';

232:   return `${anchorMessage}`;
233: }

235: function createBrokenAnchorsMessage(
236:   brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap,
237: ): string | undefined {
238:   if (Object.keys(brokenAnchors).length === 0) {
239:     return undefined;
240:   }
241: 
242:   return `Docusaurus found broken anchors!
243: 
244: Please check the pages of your site in the list below, and make sure you don't reference any anchor that does not exist.
245: Note: it's possible to ignore broken anchors with the 'onBrokenAnchors' Docusaurus configuration, and let the build pass.
246: 
247: Exhaustive list of all broken anchors found:
248: ${Object.entries(brokenAnchors)
249:   .map(([pagePath, brokenLinks]) =>
250:     createBrokenLinksMessage(pagePath, brokenLinks),
251:   )
252:   .join('\n')}
253: `;
254: }
255: 
256: function createBrokenPathsMessage(
257:   brokenPathsMap: BrokenLinksMap,
258: ): string | undefined {
259:   if (Object.keys(brokenPathsMap).length === 0) {
260:     return undefined;
261:   }
262: 
263:   /**
264:    * If there's a broken link appearing very often, it is probably a broken link
265:    * on the layout. Add an additional message in such case to help user figure
266:    * this out. See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/3567#issuecomment-706973805
267:    */
268:   function getLayoutBrokenLinksHelpMessage() {
269:     const flatList = Object.entries(brokenPathsMap).flatMap(
270:       ([pagePage, brokenLinks]) =>
271:         brokenLinks.map((brokenLink) => ({pagePage, brokenLink})),
272:     );
273: 
274:     const countedBrokenLinks = _.countBy(
275:       flatList,
276:       (item) => item.brokenLink.link,
277:     );
278: 
279:     const FrequencyThreshold = 5; // Is this a good value?
280:     const frequentLinks = Object.entries(countedBrokenLinks)
281:       .filter(([, count]) => count >= FrequencyThreshold)
282:       .map(([link]) => link);
283: 
284:     if (frequentLinks.length === 0) {
285:       return '';
286:     }
287: 
288:     return logger.interpolate`
289: 
290: It looks like some of the broken links we found appear in many pages of your site.
291: Maybe those broken links appear on all pages through your site layout?
292: We recommend that you check your theme configuration for such links (particularly, theme navbar and footer).
293: Frequent broken links are linking to:${frequentLinks}`;
294:   }
295: 
296:   return `Docusaurus found broken links!
297: 
298: Please check the pages of your site in the list below, and make sure you don't reference any path that does not exist.
299: Note: it's possible to ignore broken links with the 'onBrokenLinks' Docusaurus configuration, and let the build pass.${getLayoutBrokenLinksHelpMessage()}

301: Exhaustive list of all broken links found:
302: ${Object.entries(brokenPathsMap)
303:   .map(([pagePath, brokenPaths]) =>
304:     createBrokenLinksMessage(pagePath, brokenPaths),
305:   )
306:   .join('\n')}
307: `;
308: }
309: 
310: function splitBrokenLinks(brokenLinks: BrokenLinksMap): {
311:   brokenPaths: BrokenLinksMap;
312:   brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap;
313: } {
314:   const brokenPaths: BrokenLinksMap = {};
315:   const brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap = {};
316: 
317:   Object.entries(brokenLinks).forEach(([pathname, pageBrokenLinks]) => {
318:     const [anchorBrokenLinks, pathBrokenLinks] = _.partition(
319:       pageBrokenLinks,
320:       (link) => link.anchor,
321:     );
322: 
323:     if (pathBrokenLinks.length > 0) {
324:       brokenPaths[pathname] = pathBrokenLinks;
325:     }
326:     if (anchorBrokenLinks.length > 0) {
327:       brokenAnchors[pathname] = anchorBrokenLinks;
328:     }
329:   });
330: 
331:   return {brokenPaths, brokenAnchors};
332: }
333: 
334: function reportBrokenLinks({
335:   brokenLinks,
336:   onBrokenLinks,
337:   onBrokenAnchors,
338: }: {
339:   brokenLinks: BrokenLinksMap;
340:   onBrokenLinks: ReportingSeverity;
341:   onBrokenAnchors: ReportingSeverity;
342: }) {
343:   // We need to split the broken links reporting in 2 for better granularity
344:   // This is because we need to report broken path/anchors independently
345:   // For v3.x retro-compatibility, we can't throw by default for broken anchors
346:   // TODO Docusaurus v4: make onBrokenAnchors throw by default?
347:   const {brokenPaths, brokenAnchors} = splitBrokenLinks(brokenLinks);
348: 
349:   const pathErrorMessage = createBrokenPathsMessage(brokenPaths);
350:   if (pathErrorMessage) {
351:     logger.report(onBrokenLinks)(pathErrorMessage);
352:   }
353: 
354:   const anchorErrorMessage = createBrokenAnchorsMessage(brokenAnchors);
355:   if (anchorErrorMessage) {
356:     logger.report(onBrokenAnchors)(anchorErrorMessage);
357:   }
358: }

360: // Users might use the useBrokenLinks() API in weird unexpected ways
361: // JS users might call "collectLink(undefined)" for example
362: // TS users might call "collectAnchor('#hash')" with/without #
363: // We clean/normalize the collected data to avoid obscure errors being thrown
364: // We also use optimized data structures for a faster algorithm
365: function normalizeCollectedLinks(
366:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinks,
367: ): CollectedLinksNormalized {
368:   const result: CollectedLinksNormalized = new Map();
369:   Object.entries(collectedLinks).forEach(([pathname, pageCollectedData]) => {
370:     result.set(pathname, {
371:       links: new Set(pageCollectedData.links.filter(_.isString)),
372:       anchors: new Set(
373:         pageCollectedData.anchors
374:           .filter(_.isString)
375:           .map((anchor) => (anchor.startsWith('#') ? anchor.slice(1) : anchor)),
376:       ),
377:     });
378:   });
379:   return result;
380: }
381: 
382: export async function handleBrokenLinks({
383:   collectedLinks,
384:   onBrokenLinks,
385:   onBrokenAnchors,
386:   routes,
387: }: {
388:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinks;
389:   onBrokenLinks: ReportingSeverity;
390:   onBrokenAnchors: ReportingSeverity;
391:   routes: RouteConfig[];
392: }): Promise<void> {
393:   if (onBrokenLinks === 'ignore' && onBrokenAnchors === 'ignore') {
394:     return;
395:   }
396:   const brokenLinks = getBrokenLinks({
397:     routes,
398:     collectedLinks: normalizeCollectedLinks(collectedLinks),
399:   });

part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in `packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts`: when validating anchors, the code only looked up the target page by its exact pathname, so a link like `/docs/test#abc` failed to find the page collected as `/docs/test/` (and vice versa), even though the path itself was considered valid.

The fix (packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts:142-166): when resolving the anchor's target page, the lookup now tries the pathname plus both trailing-slash forms (encoded and decoded, deduplicated), and `isSelfTarget` is checked against all those variants as well.

Verification:
- `yarn jest packages/docusaurus/src/server/__tests__/brokenLinks.test.ts` — 35 passed (including `accepts valid non-strict link with anchor`, which covers mixed trailing-slash anchor links)
- Full `packages/docusaurus/src/server` suite — 267 passed
- `tsc --noEmit` on the `docusaurus` package — clean
